label: The School Day & the Calendar
blurb: How the year runs — the timetable, the calendar, the make-up days.
blurbZh: 一年怎麼運作——作息、行事曆、補課日。

questions.stem: Roughly when does the first semester (上學期) of a Taiwanese school year run?
options: Late August or early September to mid or late January
September to December
October to March
January to June
questions.why: The first semester runs from late August or early September to mid or late January, and the second (下學期) from mid February to the end of June. Winter vacation sits between them, timed around Lunar New Year — which is why its dates move from year to year.

questions.stem: What is 段考?
options: A staff meeting held each month
The daily cleaning period
A parent-teacher conference
A periodic exam — each semester usually has two or three, plus a final
questions.why: 段考 are the periodic exams that structure each semester. During an exam period the timetable is rewritten, and your English lesson may be shortened, moved, merged or canceled — sometimes at a day's notice.

questions.stem: You notice a Saturday marked on the school calendar as a school day. What does that mean?
options: An optional enrichment day for students who want it
A day for teachers only, with no students
A typographical error worth ignoring
A make-up school day (補課日) — a full working day you are expected to attend
questions.why: When a national holiday falls next to a weekend, Taiwan often bridges the gap and makes the day up on a Saturday. That Saturday is a normal school day: full timetable, full attendance, you included. The dates are published far in advance — which is why missing one is the least forgivable first-year mistake.

questions.stem: Which document is the authoritative source for school dates?
options: The school calendar 行事曆
Your contract
The Ministry of Education website
The school LINE group
questions.why: The 行事曆 is the source of truth; the LINE group is where same-day changes get announced, usually in Chinese; your co-teacher is who you ask when you cannot decode either. Get the calendar from 教務處 and put all of it in your phone.

questions.stem: You have designed a six-week project that builds week on week. Where should it NOT start?
options: Four weeks before an exam period, so that it runs into 段考
Immediately after a long holiday
At the beginning of a semester
In the second half of the second semester
questions.why: Anything that depends on continuity will break in an exam week — lessons get shortened, moved or canceled. Ask 教務處 for the exam dates at the start of each semester and plan your units between them, not through them.

questions.stem: Sports day (運動會) is coming. What should you expect?
options: It affects only PE lessons
It is optional for teachers who do not coach
It is often held on a Saturday, and weeks of rehearsal beforehand also take lesson time
It replaces a single afternoon
questions.why: Sports day is a whole-school event, frequently on a Saturday, and the rehearsals in the weeks before it also eat into normal lessons. Attendance is expected and being visible matters — this is one of the days colleagues remember whether you showed up.

questions.stem: Your class has a 校外教學 next Tuesday, the day you normally teach them. What happens to your lesson?
options: It is rescheduled automatically to another slot
You teach the students who did not go
It simply does not happen that week
You are required to join the trip
questions.why: A field trip is a full-day class outing and your lesson with that class does not happen. You may or may not be invited along — ask, rather than assuming either way. Plan for the loss instead of trying to recover the lesson.

questions.stem: You are told there is a 教學觀摩 and colleagues will watch one of your lessons. This is:
options: A disciplinary inspection prompted by a complaint
A routine professional activity — colleagues observe and discuss afterwards
A test that affects your contract renewal
Something you may decline without consequence
questions.why: Observed lessons are ordinary professional practice in Taiwanese schools, and being asked is not a signal that something is wrong. Ask in advance what the focus is and who will be present; treating it as normal is both accurate and the fastest way to be treated as a colleague.

questions.stem: Whether you work during winter and summer vacation is determined by:
options: Ministry of Education regulations
National holiday rules
Your contract
The homeroom teachers' rota
questions.why: Your contract decides it, and schools differ. Common arrangements include a 返校日 (return-to-school day), a winter or summer camp, or planning and preparation duties. Read the clause before you make travel plans, and confirm with 人事室 rather than with a colleague's recollection.

questions.stem: You want to take leave to fly home in April. When should you raise it?
options: A week before, so plans are still flexible
As early as you can, and before booking any flight
Only after buying the ticket, so the dates are fixed
Leave is your entitlement; no notice is needed
questions.why: Ask early, and never book flights before the leave is confirmed. Someone has to cover your classes, and requests around Lunar New Year, exam weeks and the end of term are the hardest to grant. The order matters: approval first, ticket second.

questions.stem: At 8:05 a.m. your co-teacher tells you today's lesson is canceled for a rehearsal nobody mentioned. The most useful response is:
options: Point out that you were not consulted and that this is unprofessional
Ask 教務處 to reinstate the lesson
Teach the lesson anyway in a different room
Accept it, use the time for preparation, and start asking her weekly what is changing next week
questions.why: Late notice about whole-school events is normal here and is rarely aimed at you — the information existed in Chinese somewhere upstream and did not get translated. The fix is systemic, not confrontational: ask your co-teacher once a week whether anything is changing. Ninety seconds removes most of what feels like being kept in the dark.

questions.stem: A parent meeting (親師座談會) is scheduled. What should you do?
options: Ask in advance whether you are expected to appear or introduce yourself
Ask parents to contact you directly afterwards
Prepare a full progress report on every student
Assume you are not involved unless told otherwise
questions.why: Practice varies: some schools want the foreign teacher to appear briefly and say hello, others do not involve you at all. Ask in advance rather than either turning up unexpectedly or being absent when you were expected. Individual student discussions belong to the homeroom teacher.

questions.stem: Who announces that schools are closed for a typhoon?
options: Your principal
The county or city government — for you, Changhua County
The Ministry of Education
The Central Weather Administration
questions.why: The local government announces closure, usually the evening before or by about 5:00 a.m. Check the county announcement or local news rather than relying on the school LINE group alone. If the county closes schools, you do not go in.

questions.stem: Which is the best weekly habit for staying ahead of schedule changes?
options: Checking the Ministry of Education website
Asking students what is happening
Reading the school LINE group carefully every evening
Asking your co-teacher whether anything is changing next week
questions.why: The calendar covers what was planned months ago; the LINE group covers today, usually in Chinese. The weekly question to your co-teacher covers the gap between them — which is precisely where a foreign teacher usually gets caught out.

questions.stem: 下學期 means:
options: After-school program
The lower grades
Evening classes
The second semester
questions.why: 上 = upper/first, 下 = lower/second, 學期 = semester. So 上學期 is the first semester and 下學期 the second, running from mid February to the end of June.

questions.stem: 校慶 refers to:
options: A school inspection
The school's anniversary celebration
A graduation ceremony
A staff training day
questions.why: 校 = school, 慶 = celebration. The school's birthday, sometimes combined with sports day: performances, alumni, local dignitaries, and no normal lessons.

questions.stem: 返校日 means:
options: A day students return to school during a vacation
The first day of the school year
A day for parents to visit
A make-up class on a Saturday
questions.why: 返 = return, 校 = school. A day during winter or summer vacation when students — and often staff — come in. Whether you are required to attend depends on your contract.

questions.stem: Where do you get a copy of the school calendar?
options: 人事室 Personnel Office
總務處 Office of General Affairs
教務處 Office of Academic Affairs
輔導室 Counseling Office
questions.why: 教務處 owns the calendar along with timetables, textbooks and exams. Ask in your first week of each semester — do not wait for it to be handed to you.

questions.stem: Your English lesson is canceled during an exam period. This means:
options: Your subject is not valued at this school
This is the normal rhythm of an exam week
Something has gone wrong and you should ask why
You should teach the lesson to a different class instead
questions.why: Exam periods rewrite the timetable for everyone, and it is not a comment on English or on you. The useful response is planning: get the exam dates early and build your units around them rather than into them.

questions.stem: You have planned a six-week unit. Looking at the calendar, an exam period, sports day rehearsals and a field trip will remove four of your six lessons with that class. What is the best response?
options: Teach the unit anyway and compress it into the sessions that survive
Move the unit to the second semester and teach revision until then
Redesign it as self-contained lessons that work in any order, and save the continuous unit for a clear stretch
Ask 教務處 to protect your lesson slots
questions.why: Compressing a continuous unit into fragments teaches it badly, and asking for protected slots against a whole-school event will not succeed and will cost you goodwill. Building a bank of standalone lessons for broken weeks — and saving continuous units for the clear stretches — is what experienced teachers here actually do. Read the calendar first, then design.

questions.stem: For the third time this month a lesson has been canceled at short notice, and you only found out from a student. What is the most effective thing to do?
options: Email 教務處 asking to be notified in writing of every change
Raise it with the principal as a professional-respect issue
Ask your co-teacher for a standing weekly check-in on next week's changes, and ask to be added to whichever LINE group carries the announcements
Accept it as unchangeable and stop planning in advance
questions.why: This is almost never about respect — the information existed in Chinese in a channel you are not in. Fixing the channel fixes the problem; escalating it as a grievance does not, and makes the person who could actually help you defensive. Ask for the standing check-in and the group access, and the same problem stops recurring.

questions.stem: You want two weeks of leave over Lunar New Year to travel. When and how should you handle it?
options: Book flights now while they are cheap, then request the leave
Raise it with 人事室 months ahead, confirm in writing what your contract allows during 寒假, and book only after approval
Ask a colleague what other foreign teachers have done and follow that
Wait until January, when the schedule is settled
questions.why: Lunar New Year is the hardest period to get approved, and whether you are even required to work during 寒假 is a contract question that varies by school. Get the answer in writing from 人事室 well ahead, then book. Colleagues' recollections of what someone else did are not a reliable guide to your own contract.

questions.stem: You are asked to help at sports day, which falls on a Saturday. Before agreeing, the sensible thing to establish is:
options: Whether your contract treats it as a working day, and whether compensatory time off applies — asked early and in a low-key way with 人事室
Whether you will be paid overtime, raised firmly at the time of the request
Nothing — attending school events is simply part of the job
Whether other foreign teachers are attending
questions.why: Being present at whole-school events genuinely matters to how you are seen, so start from yes. But whether a working Saturday is already counted in your hours, and whether time off in lieu applies, is a real contract question worth settling once — quietly, with 人事室, well before the day. Asked early it is administration; raised on the morning itself it reads as reluctance.

questions.stem: A make-up school day (補課日) falls on a Saturday you had already committed to something personal. What is the right move?
options: Skip it — Saturdays are not really school days
Tell your co-teacher on the Friday so somebody knows
Swap with another teacher informally
Treat it as a normal working day requiring leave: request leave as early as you can, through the normal procedure
questions.why: A 補課日 is a full working school day in every respect, so missing it needs approved leave like any other absence. The dates are published in advance precisely so this clash can be spotted early — check the whole calendar against your own commitments at the start of each semester, not the week before.
